On Tue, Sep 29, 2026 at 11:25 PM Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Liz — thanks for the heads-up and the sample traces. We see the spike in 5xx/429 across the us-west region starting ~22:55 PT.

We ran an initial triage. Findings: 
- Root cause appears to be a combination of increased tail latency on a particular GPU shard + a client-side retry library that retries on 429 without exponential backoff.
- The combination produced large inflight request queues and KV cache thrash on the shard, leading to 5xx timeouts upstream.

Temp mitigations performed (completed 00:45 PT):
- Evacuated the hot shard and drained traffic to healthy replicas (reduced 5xx baseline by ~60%).
- Applied a per-customer rate cap for BrightCart in the us-west pool to prevent client retry amplification.
- Disabled background batch compaction on the affected nodes.

Attachments: logs-20260929.tar.gz (partial kernel traces), kv-cache-dump-0929.txt

Next steps: full postmortem, long-term SLO/alert updates, and a recommended SDK change for BrightCart to use jittered exponential backoff.

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Liz — short exec update for BrightCart leadership: 
1) What happened: between 22:55–23:40 PT on 2026-09-29 a hot GPU shard experienced increased kernel tail latency while serving BrightCart inference traffic. Client libraries that retried on 429 without randomized backoff amplified load, causing queueing and 5xx errors.
2) Immediate remediation: evacuated shard, applied per-account throttling, disabled background compaction and tightened connection timeouts. These actions reduced error rate by ~75% within 30 minutes.
3) Impact: BrightCart saw ~45 minutes of degraded checkout success and increased abandonment.
4) Next actions (we will own delivery):
   - Short term (24–72h): postmortem and exec one-pager to BrightCart; SLA credit proposal; push hotfix to avoid aggressive KV cache thrash.
   - Mid term (2–4 weeks): SLO and alert tuning for shard tail latency; rate-limiter improvements to prevent retry spirals; SDK guidance for recommended backoff patterns and a patch release.
   - Long term (quarter): capacity plan for peak checkout windows across major retail customers; improved per-customer throttles in the control plane and more robust shard auto-evacuation heuristics.

Action items assigned:
- Jonas: full kernel traces, root-cause writeup, and postmortem draft (due 2026-10-02).
- Marissa: SLA credit proposal and customer comms one-pager (due 2026-10-01).
- Rishi/Hannah: alerting and SLO tuning plan + runbook link (runbook: https://redwood.app/console/runbooks/brightcart-timeout-playbook).

We will send the formal postmortem and the exec one-pager as attachments. Please let me know if BrightCart needs a bridge or an on-call exec call.

—Markus

Subject: BrightCart incident postmortem and follow-ups

Hi Liz — attached is our formal postmortem (postmortem-2026-09-30.pdf) and a short executive one-pager for your procurement and CRO. Summary highlights:
- Root cause: intersection of shard tail latency regression (kernel scheduling bug introduced in 2026-09-15 patch) and client retry behavior.
- Why the amplification happened: missing alert that correlates per-account retry rate + shard queue depth. Our current alerts were shard-centric only.
- Immediate mitigations taken: shard evacuation, per-account caps, tightened timeouts, temporarily disabled non-critical background work.

Follow-up actions (owners and due dates):
- Runbook update: create explicit runbook step to apply per-account caps during sustained 429 (>5% for 10m) — owner: Hannah, due 2026-10-07.
- Alerting: add combined alert (per-account retry-rate X shard-queue-depth) and dashboard; add mobile paging for exec on severity=1 — owner: Rishi, due 2026-10-05.
- SDK guidance: publish recommended backoff patterns and release patch v1.3.2 — owner: Developer Experience, due 2026-10-12.
- Capacity planning: update reserved capacity recommendations for retail customers with burst windows; commence Q4 capacity review — owner: Product Ops, due 2026-10-21.

We propose a 7% SLA credit for the impacted window; Marissa will follow up with procurement and include the invoice offset.

Attachments: postmortem-2026-09-30.pdf, kv-cache-dump-0929.txt

If BrightCart wants to schedule a 30-minute exec debrief next week we can set that up.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
